subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chan <lydia.chan@acme.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation and very helpful context on the product search and personalization latency targets. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist of model variants to evaluate next:

TL;DR (shortlist + rationale)
- Redwood-Generate-13B-int8 (recommended starter): balanced quality for product copy and search relevance, good latency on Dedicated pools, predictable cost.
- Llama-3-8B-q4 (open model): lowest-cost option, very good tail latency for short prompts, slightly weaker on ambiguous product descriptions — good for fast A/B tests.
- Redwood-Prod-70B-ft (high-fidelity): highest quality for complex prompt completion and multi-turn personalization; expect higher cost and longer latency, use as a fallback for high-value flows.

Why these three? During the demo we saw two core requirements: (1) 95th percentile response under 400ms on search-rewrite / ranking workloads, and (2) high fidelity for conversion-driving marketing copy. The 13B-int8 gives you a good balance for both; Llama-3-8B-q4 is a low-cost experimental path; 70B is for high-quality fallbacks and regression comparisons.

Suggested next-step evals (what we'll run together)
1) 2k prompt set run: relevance + hallucination check (we'll use the prompt_set_v1.jsonl attached).
2) Latency bench on your median query size (we'll run with your sample logs; see latency_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf for our recent infra numbers).
3) Cost delta estimates: per-1M tokens for each candidate model (ballpark in attachment).

Attachments (short): acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (side-by-side cost/latency/quality), prompt_set_v1.jsonl, latency_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf

Open questions I noted from the call:
- Security: You mentioned needing tenant isolation + KMS for keys. We can propose Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. Rafael, I flagged this for you to coordinate follow-up.
- SLA: 99.9% regionally — we can meet that with Dedicated pools and autoscaling rules.

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael (solutions): run a 2k prompt evaluation across the three candidate models and share a one-slide summary by EOD Mon (4/20).
- Marissa (me): consolidate results + pricing to share with Lydia for prioritization.
- Schedule a 30-min review next Wed to review pass/fail criteria and decide a canary path.

If that sounds good, I'll schedule the follow-up and kick off the evals — Rafael, can you confirm availability?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

---

Thanks for the clear summary and shortlist. A few quick follow-ups from my side:
1) Hallucination / factuality: do you have existing metrics (FAR/precision) for the 13B-int8 vs Llama-3-8B on product-description datasets?
2) Latency SLO: our engineering target is 95th < 400ms for search rerank (median tiny queries). Can you confirm which config you used for the 13B-int8 numbers?
3) Data handling: for the Dedicated flow, are logs accessible to our security team (audit log export)? We may need SOC2 evidence.

Also, roughly what ballpark monthly cost should we expect for a 3-node Dedicated pool at 95th SLO? We understand this is approximate.

If possible, can you include the prompt_set_v1 runs in the shared drive so our search team can preview?

Thanks — I'll review attachments and we can sync on Wed if that works.

lydia.chan@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist and next steps

Hi Lydia —

Great questions — answering inline and attaching quick references:

1) Hallucination / factuality
- Short answer: in our internal product-description evals the 13B-int8 shows a ~6-8% hallucination rate on the prompt_set_v1 baseline, Llama-3-8B-q4 sits ~9-12% (higher on long ambiguous queries). We'll run the exact numbers on your prompt set and push the results to the shared Drive folder (link below).

2) Latency SLO / config used
- The ballpark numbers in latency_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf assume: Dedicated pool on A100-equivalent GPUs, batch size tuned for median query length (~12 tokens), continuous batching enabled, and int8 kernels for the 13B. Under those conditions we see 95th percentile ~320-370ms for the 13B-int8. We'll reproduce with your exact traffic pattern.

3) Data handling and compliance
- Dedicated: full audit logs + optional audit-export to your S3 (we'll provide SOC 2 artifact pack). Private: air-gapped and KMS-integration options if you need keys in your control. Rafael — I'll route your security team the SOC2 evidence pack and the logging export doc.

Ballpark cost (3-node Dedicated pool, estimated sustained throughput matching your demo)
- Llama-3-8B-q4: ~$6k-8k / month (lowest)
- Redwood-Generate-13B-int8: ~$18k-24k / month (balanced)
- Redwood-Prod-70B-ft: ~$75k-110k / month (high quality, high cost)

I've uploaded the raw run templates and the prompt_set_v1 to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDef-ACME-Model-Evals
Benchmark doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-latency-q2-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/ACME-7621

Next steps I will take this afternoon: run the 2k prompt_set_v1 baseline across the three candidate models (Rafael will run the Dedicated configs) and push results to the Drive by EOD Tue. Can you confirm who from your search team should get the Drive access?

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachment notes: I included a quick XLSX with the side-by-side comparisons (acme_model_shortlist.xlsx). The latency PDF has recent infra numbers we used as reference.
